dialog.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
dialog.request.title: Request a broker
dialog.request.text: We're aiming to cover the most frequently used brokers in Switzerland that charge for tax statements. No guarantees or promises — but your input helps prioritize.
dialog.request.ways: Two ways to request a broker:
faq.q1: What is Open Swiss Tax Statement?
faq.a1: A free, open-source tool that generates official eCH-0196 tax statement PDFs from your broker's CSV export. Swiss cantonal tax authorities process these electronically — exactly like the statements brokers charge CHF 85–100 for.
faq.a2: Switzerland uses an open standard called eCH-0196 for electronic tax statements. This app reads your broker's transaction data, enriches it with official ESTV tax values and exchange rates, then generates a PDF with machine-readable barcodes that your tax office can scan — the same format your broker would produce.
faq.q3: Does any of my data leave my computer?
faq.a3: No. The app runs 100% offline. All parsing, enrichment, and PDF generation happens locally. There are no network calls, no analytics, no telemetry. You can verify this — the test suite includes an automated check that scans all source code for network imports.
faq.a4: Everything is stored in ~/Documents/OpenSwissTaxStatement/. Generated PDFs and input files are archived in the statements/ subfolder. All data stays on your computer and can be deleted manually at any time.
faq.q5: Will this work for next year's tax statement?
faq.a5: The app needs yearly updates for ESTV exchange rates and the ICTAX Kursliste (official security tax values). These are bundled with each release. As long as the eCH-0196 standard remains unchanged and updated data is available, it will work for future years.
faq.a6: Currently Swissquote (full support). More Swiss brokers are planned — see the landing page for the roadmap.
faq.a7: Three categories in ~/Documents/OpenSwissTaxStatement/: statements/ — generated PDFs and copies of your input files, organized by year. data/ — user-provided Kursliste overrides (only when the bundled data doesn’t cover your tax year). preferences.json — app preferences like your saved profile.
faq.q8: How does the DA-1 form (foreign withholding tax) work?
faq.a8: The app automatically fills in DA-1 data for foreign dividends (Rubrik B). It uses ESTV’s official DA-1 rate tables to calculate the non-recoverable withholding tax and lump-sum tax credit for each country. Investment funds (ETFs, index funds) use the same DA-1 rates as shares, since fund distributions are treated as dividend income under tax treaties. After importing the tax statement into your cantonal tax software, make sure to select «Yes» on the DA-1 claim question — otherwise the pre-filled DA-1 entries won’t appear.
faq.a9: The app has been tested with real Swissquote data covering: shares (Swiss and foreign), ETFs and investment funds, dividends with Swiss withholding tax (Rubrik A) and foreign withholding tax (Rubrik B / DA-1), cash balances in CHF, EUR, and USD, and German and English Swissquote PDF exports. Not yet tested: bonds, structured products, options/warrants, French and Italian Swissquote exports, and brokers other than Swissquote. If you encounter issues with untested scenarios, please report them on GitHub.
faq.q10: How do I export my files from Swissquote?
faq.a10:
You need two files from Swissquote:

1. Transaction File (CSV or Kontoauszug PDF)
For CSV: Log in to Swissquote → Transactions → set the date range to cover the full tax year (01.01–31.12) → click Export.
For Kontoauszug: Go to e-Documents → download the account statement (Kontoauszug) PDF for the tax year.

2. Portfolio PDF
Go to Reports → Portfolio Valuation (Portfolio-Wertentwicklung) → select the year-end date (31.12) → download the PDF.

The portfolio PDF provides year-end holdings, cash balances, and your personal details. Both files together give the app everything it needs to generate a complete tax statement.
